input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only provision giving HDI a right to inspect our records; there is no other audit, verification or system-access right in the Agreement. The notice (30 days' prior written), business-hours limitation and cost allocation (HDI bears its inspection costs unconditionally, with no underpayment trigger) already meet or exceed the fallback. However, the clause imposes no limit on how often HDI may inspect, which is unlimited-frequency audit territory and fails the fallback on a material term. We have therefore made the single minimal edit needed to add the once-per-year cap, targeting the fallback level; the preferred independent-auditor, off-site and no-system-access refinements are not pursued because the clause is a records inspection only and would require collateral rewrites.

proposal.summary: Cap HDI's inspection right at once per year
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 3.4 gives HDI an unlimited-frequency right to inspect our records, so we have added the playbook's once-per-year cap; the existing 30 days' written notice, business-hours limit and HDI-borne costs already satisfy our position.
